inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement, and is threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are not met. This looks less like an isolated labor dispute than a pressure game: years of delay have left universities exposed, while officials can now portray any disruption as the unions’ fault rather than answer for the stalled talks. The ultimatum came from SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council—but the real question is who benefits from keeping the dispute unresolved.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month deadline to renegotiate the 2009 agreement feels less like a genuine route to resolution than a carefully useful countdown. After years of delay, officials can let tensions build, then point to an indefinite nationwide strike and claim the unions caused the damage. The ultimatum from SSANU’s 54th National Executive Council may be real, but the bigger question is whether powerful interests are content to keep the talks stalled while the blame gets redirected.
